lines.t: This is Nexa.
A planet where almost every person awakens a power — a quirk, a gift, a weapon.
On Nexa, power is everything. The strongest live in luxury houses, receive free premium services, and walk through doors that open only for them.
The weak are tolerated. The powerless are not. They are sent to the labour districts, to build the towers the strong will live in.
Seventeen years ago, Nexa's No. 1 hero — Richard Parker — was the strongest man alive. One punch could end any fight. His body moved on instinct alone.
Beside him fought Elena Parker, the second-strongest hero, whose barriers could hold back a storm.
Then came ZERO.
Your planet has such interesting power. I think I'll take it.
Richard fought Zero across three continents. In the end, he struck him down — and vanished in the light of the final blow.
The world mourned its hero. It did not know the truth: Zero had survived, absorbed Richard's power, and sealed him away on a distant planet.
Within a year, Zero ruled Nexa. The heroes who remained learned to kneel — or disappeared.
Elena was given government housing 'in honour of her service'. A polite cage, with a view of the labour trucks.
She raised their son alone.
His name is Peter Parker. He is sixteen years old.
He is top of his class in every written exam… and last in every power trial.
Because Peter Parker — son of the two strongest heroes on Nexa — was born powerless.

CHAPTER 1
Powerless
Peter! Breakfast! If you're late again, Professor Hale will call me, and then I will be forced to embarrass you.
I'm up, I'm up. …Is that egg on toast? You never make egg on toast.
It's the first day of the trial week. I thought you could use something special.
The trial week. Another week of everyone watching me lose.
Peter. Look at me. Whatever happens today, your power doesn't decide who you are.

choice.t: "Easy to say when you're the second-strongest hero on the planet."
"I know, Mom. I'll do my best."

lines.t: …Was. Was the second-strongest. Now I'm just your mother. Which is a much harder job.
Sorry. I didn't mean it.
I know. Eat.
That's all anyone can ask. Your father used to say the same thing before every fight.
Your father? …All the time, when he was young. He'd get up, dust himself off, and try again the next morning.
That was his real power, if you ask me.
Now go. And Peter — if those crew kids touch you, you tell me.
And then what? You'll put them in a barrier bubble?
Don't tempt me.
